newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria suffers fall in Russian gas supplies.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria suffers fall in Russian gas supplies.

text.p: Bulgaria has started curbing Russian natural gas supplies to some of its biggest industrial plants due to a cold spell and increased gas consumption in Eastern Europe, gas monopolist Bulgargas said on Sunday.
"Natural gas supplies to Bulgaria and volumes running to Turkey have been proportionally reduced," a Bulgargas statement said.
Bulgaria and Turkey get Russian gas through a pipeline, transiting Russia, Ukraine and Romania.

Supplies are being reduced to 25 out of the 160 industrial consumers in the country, the statement said. They are chemical, cement and central heating plants, including the country's biggest steel works of Kremikovtsi, it added.
Bulgargas officials declined to give further details on gas pipeline pressure and current daily volume of deliveries.
Supplies to Bulgaria, which is totally dependent on Russia for its gas imports, are expected to be back to normal on January 3, the statement said.
Officials said many plants did not work at full capacity during the season's holidays.
Last winter, Bulgaria and Turkey were badly hurt by lower Russian gas flows.
